svg.title: GamingMaster: two agents by decision latency
svg.desc: A game is routed by how long one decision may take. Meta-Harness: every game is played by Astra, a reasoning model, and Jev, a fast System-1 model, through a harness program generated for that game; the game is either turn-based or real-time, and in a real-time game the low-latency decisions go to Jev or to code while Astra plans in the background. Multi-game network: a trained network with a shared core acts every frame. The Meta-Harness builds its harnesses from a game's name; the network is trained by joint imitation learning, then mixed-game reinforcement learning.
svg.text: How long may one decision take before the game punishes it?
a second or less: the world keeps ticking
Meta-Harness · every game gets Astra + Jev
the pace comes with the game
puzzles, cards, board and text games
one trained network, one forward per frame
the core is shared by every game
a coding model writes, tests and improves the harness program
